title: How to set Chrome as default browser on Mac: steps for macOS Ventura and later
metaTitle: How to Set Chrome as Default Browser on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to set Chrome as default browser on Mac from Chrome Settings or System Settings, plus fixes when Chrome is missing from the list.
targetKeyword: how to set chrome as default browser on mac
secondaryKeywords: system settings default web browser mac
intro: To set Chrome as your default browser on Mac, open Chrome, click the three dots at the top right, choose Settings, then click Make default. You can also choose Apple menu > System Settings > Desktop & Dock, then pick Google Chrome under Default web browser.
tldr: Open Chrome, click the three dots at the top right, choose Settings, find Default browser, and click Make default.
Click Use “Chrome” in the macOS prompt to confirm the change. No Make default button means Chrome is already your default.
On macOS Ventura 13 or later, Apple menu > System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Default web browser also works.
Mail has its own default. Change it in Mail > Settings > General > Default email reader.
If Chrome is missing from the list, launch it fully, confirm it sits in Applications, then restart your Mac.

blocks.text: Two routes, one setting

Chrome and macOS both control the default browser, and both routes end at the same setting. The Chrome route starts inside the browser. The macOS route starts in System Settings, so you can use it from anywhere on the Mac. Pick whichever one you can reach faster.

rows: More (three dots) > Settings > Default browser > Make default
Inside Chrome. Confirm with Use “Chrome” in the macOS prompt.
Apple menu > System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Default web browser
macOS Ventura 13 or later. Older macOS uses System Preferences > General.
blocks.caption: Both routes change which browser opens web links. Mail keeps a separate setting.

blocks.text: Set Chrome as default from Chrome Settings

Open Chrome and look at the top right of the window. The three dots open the More menu. Choose Settings, and the Chrome settings page opens. Find the section named Default browser. If Chrome is not your default yet, a Make default button appears there. Click it, then click Use “Chrome” in the macOS prompt that follows.
Setapp's guide also describes the same page as Chrome > Settings in the menu bar. Use whichever path you find first. Both lead to the Default browser section, so the rest of the steps stay the same.
Set Chrome as default from System Settings
Apple's steps apply to macOS Ventura 13 or later. They work whether or not you already have Chrome open. Follow the list below in order.

items: Click the Apple menu in the top left corner, then choose System Settings.
Click Desktop & Dock in the sidebar.
Scroll down to Default web browser and open the menu.
Choose Google Chrome from the list.

blocks.text: Setapp says the change takes effect immediately. Apple's wording is more cautious. It says some third-party browsers and webmail services keep their own link settings, and it does not spell out how every link type behaves.
Older macOS versions

Apple's older steps use System Preferences instead of System Settings. Open the Apple menu, choose System Preferences, and click General. Then open the Default web browser menu and pick Google Chrome. Expect the same result as the newer route, with different menu names.
What changes when Chrome is the default browser

Apps that open web links now send them to Chrome. That covers links you click in Notes and most other apps that open websites. Safari stays on your Mac. Changing the setting does not remove it, so you can switch back at any time.

Some apps keep their own link settings. Apple points out that some third-party browsers and webmail services handle links on their own. If one app still opens Safari after you change the setting, look in that app's preferences before you blame macOS.
Mail uses its own default

Chrome does not control email links. Mail has a separate setting. Open Mail, choose Mail > Settings, click General, then set Default email reader. Apple says email links open in Mail by default, so leave it alone if Mail works for you.
When Chrome is missing from the list

If Chrome does not appear in the Default web browser menu, work through these checks in order. Setapp's guide lists them. It does not mention specific error codes, so the fix is a sequence of checks rather than a single setting.

items: Launch Chrome fully at least once.
Check that Chrome is in Applications, not Downloads. Drag it into Applications if it is somewhere else.
Restart your Mac, then open the Default web browser menu again.
Reinstall Chrome from google.com/chrome if the list still does not show it.

blocks.text: When the setting keeps switching back

Some people report that the default browser changes back to another app. Those reports come from forums. Official Apple and Google pages do not cover this, so treat these fixes as things to try, not guarantees.

items: Restart your Mac, then update Chrome.
Look for a second copy of Chrome, such as one in Downloads. Keep the copy in Applications and remove the others.
If your Mac belongs to a work or school, a managed setting may control the default. Ask your IT team before you change it.

blocks.text: How common Chrome is, and what the numbers do not show

Chrome is the most used desktop browser in the world. StatCounter measured it at 66.98% of worldwide desktop browser use in October 2026. That figure covers every desktop system, so it does not show how many Macs run Chrome.

A Mozilla study of about 12,000 people in Germany, Spain and Poland found that 98% of people who picked a browser on a choice screen expected to keep it. Those are stated expectations, not switching you can observe. Read the number as a hint, not proof.
Check that the change worked
Open Notes, paste a web address, and click the link. Chrome should open it. If Safari opens instead, go back to the setting and confirm that Google Chrome is still selected.
You can also return to Chrome Settings. If the Make default button is gone, Google says Chrome is already your default browser. That is the result you want.
Mistakes people make

items: Changing Mail and expecting web links to follow. Mail and web browsers have separate defaults.
Skipping the macOS prompt. Setapp's steps include the Use “Chrome” click, so do not skip it.
Hunting for a Make default button after the change already worked. A missing button means Chrome is already the default.
Running Chrome from Downloads. Move it to Applications first so macOS lists it.
Assuming one app's setting controls every link. Some apps keep their own link settings.

blocks.text: Set Chrome as default on Windows or Android

Google's help page covers other systems too. On Windows 11, open Start > Settings > Apps > Default apps, search for Chrome, select Google Chrome, then click Set default next to Make Google Chrome your default browser.
On Android, open Chrome, tap More, then tap Make Chrome default and select the button next to Chrome. Google's guide says its Mac and Linux steps match the desktop steps on this page.
Keep Chrome current

Google says Chrome releases a new update every four weeks. Its Chrome Releases blog posted a Stable Channel update for desktop on October 29, 2026. The sources checked did not give a current version number, so this page does not name one.
If the default setting behaves oddly, update Chrome, then retry the steps above. A current browser is the simplest thing to rule out.

faq.question: Do I need to change Mail too?
faq.answer: Only if you want email links to open somewhere other than Mail. Mail has its own default. Open Mail, choose Mail > Settings, click General, and set Default email reader. Apple says email links open in Mail by default, and changing Chrome does not change that.

faq.question: Why is there no Make default button in Chrome?
faq.answer: Google's help page says that if the button is missing, Chrome is already your default browser. Check the Default web browser menu in System Settings to confirm Google Chrome is selected, then move on.

faq.question: Does making Chrome the default remove Safari?
faq.answer: No. Safari stays on your Mac. Apple says changing the default browser changes which browser opens web links. To switch back, use the same menu you used to pick Chrome.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to set Chrome as default on Mac?
faq.answer: The Apple and Google pages checked list menu steps only, so this page uses menus. Chrome's Settings page is the place to look if you want to find one.

faq.question: Does this work on older versions of macOS?
faq.answer: Apple's System Settings steps apply to macOS Ventura 13 or later. On earlier versions, open System Preferences, click General, and use the Default web browser menu. Chrome's own Make default steps are the same on Mac and Linux, according to Google.

faq.question: Why did Chrome stop being my default browser?
faq.answer: Forum reports describe the setting switching back after restarts or updates. Official Apple and Google pages do not explain this. Restart your Mac, update Chrome, remove duplicate copies, and check whether a managed setting controls your Mac.

faq.question: Will changing the default affect a work or school Mac?
faq.answer: It might. A managed Mac can have settings that control the default browser. Ask your IT team before you change it, so the change does not get reversed by a policy later.

task: Set Chrome as the default browser on Mac
appliesTo: Google Chrome on macOS Ventura 13 or later, with notes for older macOS versions
requirements: A Mac running macOS Ventura 13 or later for the System Settings steps
Google Chrome installed in the Applications folder
Chrome opened fully at least once so it appears in the macOS list

steps.name: Open Chrome
steps.text: Open Google Chrome from the Applications folder or the Dock. Wait for the window to appear before you go on.
steps.tip: Setapp's troubleshooting says to confirm Chrome is in Applications, not Downloads.

steps.name: Open the More menu
steps.text: Look at the top right of the Chrome window and click the three dots. Google calls this the More menu.
steps.tip: Setapp describes the same place as Chrome > Settings in the menu bar.

steps.name: Choose Settings
steps.text: Click Settings. Chrome opens its settings page.
steps.tip: The next step is in the Default browser section of this page.

steps.name: Find Default browser
steps.text: Find the section named Default browser on the Settings page. Google's help page uses that exact label.
steps.tip: Match the wording on your screen if the layout looks different.

steps.name: Click Make default
steps.text: Click Make default in the Default browser section. This starts the change.
steps.tip: No Make default button? Google says Chrome is already your default browser. You can stop here.

steps.name: Confirm in the macOS prompt
steps.text: macOS asks you to confirm. Click Use “Chrome” in the prompt.
steps.tip: If you close the prompt without confirming, repeat the Make default step.

steps.name: Test with a web link
steps.text: Open Notes, paste a web address, and click it. Chrome should open the page.
steps.tip: Test with a web link, not an email link. Email links open in Mail by default.

troubleshooting.problem: Chrome is missing from the Default web browser list
troubleshooting.fix: Launch Chrome fully at least once, confirm it is in Applications and not Downloads, then restart your Mac. Reinstall from google.com/chrome if it still does not appear.

troubleshooting.problem: No Make default button in Chrome Settings
troubleshooting.fix: Chrome is already your default browser, according to Google. Confirm in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Default web browser that Google Chrome is selected.

troubleshooting.problem: Web links still open in Safari after the change
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether the app that opened the link has its own link setting. Apple says some apps do. Then confirm the change in System Settings and try the link again.

troubleshooting.problem: The default switches back to another browser
troubleshooting.fix: Forum reports suggest restarting, updating Chrome, removing duplicate copies, and checking for a managed setting. Official sources do not confirm these fixes.

troubleshooting.problem: Email links open in Mail, not Chrome
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected. Mail has its own default. Change it in Mail > Settings > General > Default email reader if you want a different app.
